newsitem.title: PERU: Peru grants Easter pardons to 91 common criminals.
newsitem.headline: Peru grants Easter pardons to 91 common criminals.

text.p: Peru granted Easter pardons on Wednesday to 91 prisoners whose sentences were unrelated to crimes committed by any of the country's two leftist rebel groups, officials said.
A Justice Ministry resolution published in the official gazette El Peruano said five women and 86 men held at medium and minimum security facilities in Lima and the provinces were being released.

The publication of a pardons list initially sparked speculation it might be tied to a possible deal between the government and Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence since Dec. 19.

But this was denied by members of an ad hoc commission created last year to review cases of those unjustly jailed on terrorism and treason charges for alleged links to Maoist Shining Path or Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebel groups. About 5,000 Peruvians are behind bars on charges of terrorism or treason.

"There is a custom here in Peru that prisoners are pardoned for Mother's Day, Independence Day and other holidays," the Rev. Hubert Lanssiers, a Roman Catholic priest and member of the ad hoc panel, said.
"This is routine and exclusively for common criminals. It has nothing to do with the commission," he added.
About 20 MRTA rebels who stormed the Japanese ambassador's home on Dec. 19 are demanding the release of 450 jailed comrades.
